summary: A ground-rooted woody vine attaches to bark with adhesive root pads. Climbing routes require stems at least 4 cm thick with multiple intact attachments and sound host support. Vertical reach never exceeds the actual host: at most 22 m on nieblon or 32 m on madre_de_agua. Soft fruit rewards dispersers; red-veined leaves warn of alkaloids (F18, F19, F25).

chains.trait: Adhesive roots and mature woody cables
links: Established trees supply support toward canopy light.
Attachment roots fasten the vine while ground roots supply water.
Woody thickening and repeated attachments distribute loads.
The host's structure and height set the climbing route's limits.
chains.play: Climb only stems at least 4 cm in diameter with multiple intact bark attachments and sound supporting branches.
chains.weakness: Thin shoots, detached loops and failing host branches cannot reliably bear a creature.
observe: A thick cable remains attached at several separate points.
A fallen host branch brings its attached vine down.

plausibility.summary: A diameter of at least 4 cm and multiple intact attachments are necessary route conditions, not universal load guarantees. Vertical reach is capped by the actual host, with upper bounds of 22 m on nieblon and 32 m on madre_de_agua.

analogues.mechanism: Attachment rootlets permit ascent on existing supports; creature-bearing mature cables are a restricted fictional extension.

chains.trait: Defended foliage and separate fruit rewards
links: Persistent leaves benefit from alkaloid defence.
Ripe fruit softens and becomes fragrant.
Alula and rondo move seeds while feeding on pulp.
chains.play: Choose fruit by softness and scent while avoiding defended leaves.
chains.weakness: Soft fruit spoils rapidly and wind disperses scent cues.
observe: Red-veined leaves remain firm beside ripe fruit.
Ripe fruit yields while unripe fruit stays hard.
Seeds appear beneath feeding perches and along rondo routes.

plausibility.summary: Fruit rewards do not reverse the red-purple foliage warning. Scent persistence applies in still sheltered air.

analogues.mechanism: Chemical and structural differences between foliage and pulp can defend persistent tissues while rewarding seed dispersers.

poison.signal: Red-veined leaves warn of alkaloids; ripe pulp is identified by softness and scent.

gameplay.nest_material: Fine fallen stems and detached fibres.
gameplay.notes: Enable climbing only on stems at least 4 cm thick with multiple intact bark attachments and sound host support. Cap every route at actual host height; unsupported loops are not independent aerial cables.

relations.note: Eats ripe canopy fruit and uses supported stems between perches.
Eats fallen pulp and transports surviving seeds.
Climbs eligible multiply attached mature stems and gathers ripe fruit.
Uses the host as support; vertical reach cannot exceed its actual height or 22 m.
Can climb the single spring giant up to its actual height, never above 32 m.

generator.trunk: Ground-rooted woody cable, 4–12 cm thick when mature; juvenile shoots are thinner. Vertical reach follows the actual supporting host.

branching.buttress: None; root pads attach at repeated bark contacts.

overlay_rules: Fruit remains muted green to cream while softening and developing scent.

placement.slope: Stable sheltered woodland slopes and banks with established woody hosts.
placement.soil: Humus-filled volcanic soil and deep bank crevices.
placement.fog: Frequent fog supports humid attachment surfaces.
placement.density: Scattered rooted vines; clamp vertical reach to actual host height, at most 22 m on nieblon and 32 m on madre_de_agua. Shorter hosts impose lower caps.

generator.seasonal: Evergreen where moist; wet periods support shoot growth and warm seasons bring patchy fruit crops.
generator.wind_response: Leaves streamline and lateral shoots flex; exposed unsupported spans can break.

journal.en: The thick ropes climb the trees. Soft fruit smells sweet; red-veined leaves stay bitter.
journal.es: Las sogas gruesas trepan por los árboles. El fruto blando huele dulce; las hojas de venas rojas siguen amargas.
